propositions.text: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the RAD decision upholding the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The Applicant seeks judicial review pursuant to subsection 72(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 [IRPA], of a decision by the Refugee Appeal Division [RAD] of the Immigration and Refugee Board, wherein the RAD upheld a decision of the Refugee Protection Division [RPD] that the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant seeks judicial review of the RAD decision upholding the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim.

propositions.text: The Applicant, Didier Mauricio Valdebanquez Ortiz, is a 32-year-old Colombian citizen.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, Didier Mauricio Valdebanquez Ortiz (age 32), is a citizen of Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant is a 32-year-old Colombian citizen.

propositions.text: The Applicant alleges persecution by FARC in Bogota, including demands for drugs and beatings after refusal.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, a pharmacist, alleges that he was persecuted by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia - People's Army [FARC] in Bogota. In October 2012, the FARC demanded large quantities of drugs from the Applicant; and, when the Applicant refused, he and his cousin – who worked for him at the pharmacy, were both beaten.

propositions.text: The Applicant's common law spouse received threatening phone calls after the beatings.
propositions.quote: Thereafter, the Applicant’s common law spouse received threatening telephone calls.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant alleges FARC persecution including drug demands, beatings, and threats to his spouse.

propositions.text: The Applicant moved his pharmacy in November 2012 but was again persecuted by FARC.
propositions.quote: In November 2012, the Applicant moved his pharmacy to another neighbourhood in Bogota; but, was again persecuted by the FARC.

propositions.text: In April 2013, the Applicant was kidnapped, stabbed, and required surgery, supported by medical and police reports.
propositions.quote: In April 2013, the Applicant was allegedly kidnapped by FARC members. He was stabbed and needed surgery. The Applicant submitted as evidence, before the RPD, a medical report and a police report related to the incident.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant alleges kidnapping and stabbing by FARC in 2013, supported by medical and police reports.

propositions.text: After another FARC threat, the Applicant moved to Riochacha, returned to Bogota where his cousin was killed in a shooting, then hid in Bucaramanga for five months.
propositions.quote: After receiving another threatening note from the FARC, the Applicant moved to the city of Riochacha on May 26, 2013. He returned to Bogota on July 22, 2013; and, while in Bogota with his cousin, someone shot at them. His cousin was killed. On August 1, 2013, the Applicant moved to Bucaramanga and hid there for five months.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant moved due to threats, his cousin was killed in Bogota, and he hid in Bucaramanga for five months.

propositions.text: The Applicant returned to Bogota to apply for a US visa, fled to the US, then entered Canada illegally with help, claiming asylum.
propositions.quote: On January 20, 2014, the Applicant returned to Bogota to apply for a visa for the United States; and, fled to the United States on May 17, 2014. On June 2, 2014, the Applicant illegally entered to Canada allegedly with the assistance of a stranger he had met in a train station in New York. The Applicant claimed asylum in Canada on June 18, 2014.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant fled Colombia to the US, then entered Canada illegally and claimed asylum.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the Applicant’s refugee claim due to doubts about key allegations and contradictions in testimony.
propositions.quote: In a decision dated November 5, 2014, the RPD rejected the Applicant’s claim for refugee status. The RPD had doubts in respect of the veracity of allegations central to the Applicant’s narrative.

propositions.text: The RPD did not believe the Applicant changed his business location to escape FARC threats.
propositions.quote: Namely, the RPD did not believe that the Applicant had to change his place of business in order to escape the alleged threats of the FARC;

propositions.text: The Applicant contradicted himself about why his cousin stayed in Bogota despite threats.
propositions.quote: the Applicant contradicted himself during his testimony as to why his cousin decided to stay in Bogota despite the threats;

propositions.text: The RPD found it improbable that someone fearing FARC would return to Bogota to visit spouse and cousin.
propositions.quote: and, someone fearing the FARC would not return to Bogota simply to visit his common law spouse and his cousin.

propositions.text: The RPD found it improbable the Applicant paid a stranger $5,000 to help cross the Canadian border and share his story.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the RPD held that it was not probable that the Applicant decided to pay a stranger, met coincidentally in a train station in New York, $5,000 to help him cross the Canadian border; and, entrust him with his story.

propositions.text: Due to doubts about key allegations, the RPD gave no probative weight to supporting documents including medical and death certificates.
propositions.quote: Moreover, given RPD’s doubts regarding allegations central to the narrative of the Applicant, the RPD gave no probative weight to several supporting documents, including: a surgical report, the death certificate of his cousin; as well as medical and police reports.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claim due to doubts about key allegations, contradictions, and gave no weight to supporting documents.

propositions.text: The Applicant and his spouse's refugee claims were joined for hearing before the RPD; the Applicant appealed to RAD; spouse sought judicial review.
propositions.quote: The refugee status claim of the Applicant, and his common law spouse, Maryori Umana Rodriguez, were joined for their hearing before the RPD. The Applicant appealed to the RAD; and, Ms. Rodriguez sought judicial review of the RPD’s decision.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant appealed the RPD decision to RAD; spouse sought judicial review.

propositions.text: The RAD dismissed the Applicant's appeal on April 20, 2015.
propositions.quote: In a decision dated April 20, 2015, the RAD dismissed the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismissed the Applicant's appeal.

propositions.text: The RAD intervenes on facts only for overriding and palpable errors but must independently assess evidence as a whole.
propositions.quote: The RAD was guided by Huruglica c Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2014 FC 799; the RAD stated that its role is to intervene on a determination of facts only where there is an overriding and palpable error by the RPD. Nonetheless, the RAD recognized that it must conduct an independent assessment of the evidence as a whole (see Youkap v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 FC 249).

paragraphs.summary: The RAD intervenes on facts only for overriding errors but must independently assess evidence.

propositions.text: The RAD found no error in RPD's overall determination and found the Applicant not credible on pharmacy ownership and testimony.
propositions.quote: The RAD held, after reviewing the evidence as a whole and listening to the audio record of the hearing, that the RPD did not err in its overall determination. Subsequently, the RAD held that, on the balance of probabilities, the Applicant was not credible, specifically with regard to the sale of his first pharmacy and the opening of a second pharmacy.

propositions.text: The RAD found the Applicant sold his first pharmacy only after arriving in Canada, not in 2012 as alleged.
propositions.quote: The RAD found that the Applicant only sold his first pharmacy after he was in Canada, and not in 2012 as alleged.

propositions.text: The Applicant did not provide corroborative evidence of ownership of the second pharmacy.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the Applicant did not provide any corroborative evidence of ownership in the second pharmacy.

propositions.text: The Applicant's credibility was affected by inconsistent and difficult testimony requiring repeated questioning.
propositions.quote: The credibility of the Applicant was furthermore affected by his difficult testimony before the RPD, during which the Applicant changed his answers, and, the questions had to be asked numerous times.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found the Applicant not credible on pharmacy ownership and inconsistent testimony.

propositions.text: The RPD was not required to address every document; RAD upheld RPD's rejection of documents without analysis of genuineness.
propositions.quote: Regarding the fact that the RPD did not give probative weight to official documents without analysis or evidence or a statement in respect of the genuineness of the documents; the RAD held that the RPD was not bound to address each and every document.

propositions.text: The RAD dismissed the appeal and upheld the RPD's decision that the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: As a result of the foregoing, the RAD dismissed the appeal; and, upheld the RPD’s decision that the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD upheld RPD's rejection of documents and dismissed the appeal, confirming the Applicant is not a refugee.

propositions.text: Did the RAD err in upholding RPD’s credibility findings?
propositions.quote: 1. Did the RAD err in upholding RPD’s credibility findings?

propositions.text: Did the RAD breach procedural fairness by making new negative credibility findings without opportunity to respond?
propositions.quote: 2. Did the RAD breach procedural fairness by having made new negative credibility findings against the Applicant without having provided the parties an opportunity to address the RPD’s concerns?

paragraphs.summary: The Court must decide if the RAD erred on credibility or breached procedural fairness by new findings without notice.

propositions.text: Sections 96 and 97 of IRPA define Convention refugee and person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: The following are the relevant legislative provisions: Convention refugee Définition de « réfugié » 96. A Convention refugee is a person who, by reason of a well-founded fear of persecution for reasons of race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group or political opinion, 96. A qualité de réfugié au sens de la Convention — le réfugié — la personne qui, craignant avec raison d’être persécutée du fait de sa race, de sa religion, de sa nationalité, de son appartenance à un groupe social ou de ses opinions politiques : (a) is outside each of their countries of nationality and is unable or, by reason of that fear, unwilling to avail themself of the protection of each of those countries; or a) soit se trouve hors de tout pays dont elle a la nationalité et ne peut ou, du fait de cette crainte, ne veut se réclamer de la protection de chacun de ces pays; (b) not having a country of nationality, is outside the country of their former habitual residence and is unable or, by reason of that fear, unwilling to return to that country. b) soit, si elle n’a pas de nationalité et se trouve hors du pays dans lequel elle avait sa résidence habituelle, ne peut ni, du fait de cette crainte, ne veut y retourner. Person in need of protection Personne à protéger 97. (1) A person in need of protection is a person in Canada whose removal to their country or countries of nationality or, if they do not have a country of nationality, their country of former habitual residence, would subject them personally 97. (1) A qualité de personne à protéger la personne qui se trouve au Canada et serait personnellement, par son renvoi vers tout pays dont elle a la nationalité ou, si elle n’a pas de nationalité, dans lequel elle avait sa résidence habituelle, exposée : (a) to a danger, believed on substantial grounds to exist, of torture within the meaning of Article 1 of the Convention Against Torture; or a) soit au risque, s’il y a des motifs sérieux de le croire, d’être soumise à la torture au sens de l’article premier de la Convention contre la torture; (b) to a risk to their life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if b) soit à une menace à sa vie ou au risque de traitements ou peines cruels et inusités dans le cas suivant : (i) the person is unable or, because of that risk, unwilling to avail themself of the protection of that country, (i) elle ne peut ou, de ce fait, ne veut se réclamer de la protection de ce pays, (ii) the risk would be faced by the person in every part of that country and is not faced generally by other individuals in or from that country, (ii) elle y est exposée en tout lieu de ce pays alors que d’autres personnes originaires de ce pays ou qui s’y trouvent ne le sont généralement pas, (iii) the risk is not inherent or incidental to lawful sanctions, unless imposed in disregard of accepted international standards, and (iii) la menace ou le risque ne résulte pas de sanctions légitimes — sauf celles infligées au mépris d

paragraphs.summary: Sections 96 and 97 of IRPA define Convention refugee and person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The RAD erred in upholding RPD’s credibility findings on pharmacy ownership.
propositions.quote: The Applicant submits that the RAD erred in upholding RPD’s credibility findings regarding the ownership of the first pharmacy.

propositions.text: The RAD erred in rejecting corroborative documents without evidence of invalidity, citing Halili.
propositions.quote: Secondly, it was a reviewable error for the RAD to have upheld the RPD’s decision to reject documents, used as corroborative documents, in the absence of evidence tending to show their invalidity (Halili v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2002 FCT 999).

propositions.text: The RAD erred in upholding RPD’s findings that the Applicant lacked subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Thirdly, the RAD erred in upholding the RPD’s findings that the Applicant lacked subjective fear.

propositions.text: The RAD breached procedural fairness by making new negative inferences without giving the Applicant a chance to respond, citing Dundar.
propositions.quote: Fourthly, it was unfair for the RAD to make a negative inference regarding the police report, and the death certificate, without the RAD having put forward to the Applicant its concerns, as these were not raised before the RPD (see Dundar v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2007 FC 1026 at paras 19-22); thus, the RAD breached procedural fairness.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues RAD erred on credibility, document rejection, subjective fear, and breached procedural fairness by new negative inferences.

propositions.text: The onus is on the Applicant to establish his claim; RAD can analyze evidence and find it lacking if supporting evidence is missing.
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the onus is on the Applicant to establish his claim. The RAD is entitled to conduct its own analysis of the evidence before the RPD; it is not an error for the RAD to find an applicant’s evidence lacking when an applicant fails to submit supporting evidence that could have been obtained (Reyna Flores v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2010 FC 874 at para 9; section 11 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227).

propositions.text: The RAD did not err in upholding RPD’s findings on the Applicant’s lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the RAD did not err in upholding the RPD’s findings in regard to the lack of subjective fear of the Applicant.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent argues the onus is on the Applicant; RAD properly analyzed evidence and did not err on subjective fear findings.

propositions.text: RAD’s decision on RPD’s credibility findings is reviewed for reasonableness with deference to RPD.
propositions.quote: The RAD’s decision to uphold RPD’s credibility findings is reviewable on the standard of review of reasonableness; and, the RAD has a duty of deference regarding the credibility findings of the RPD as the RPD has had the opportunity to hear the witness (Koffi v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 4 [Koffi]).

propositions.text: Procedural fairness breach by RAD making new findings without notice is reviewed on correctness standard.
propositions.quote: Whether the RAD breached procedural fairness by making additional credibility findings without sharing those concerns with the parties must be reviewed on the standard of correctness (Husian v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 FC 684 [Husian]).

paragraphs.summary: The Court reviews RAD’s credibility findings for reasonableness and procedural fairness breaches for correctness.

propositions.text: RAD owes high deference to RPD’s credibility findings as RPD hears witnesses and observes demeanor.
propositions.quote: The RAD correctly held that it owes a high level of deference towards RPD’s findings of credibility. As explained by Justice Mary J. L. Gleason, in Rahal v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2012 FC 319 at para 42, the RPD has “the advantage of hearing the witnesses testify, observed their demeanor and is alive to all the factual nuances and contradictions in the evidence”.

propositions.text: The RPD found inconsistencies and lack of corroboration in the Applicant’s testimony and evidence regarding his cousin, pharmacies, spouse, and border crossing.
propositions.quote: In the present case, the RAD upheld RPD’s findings of lack of credibility of the Applicant; specifically, the RPD had held that: • The Applicant’s testimony was inconsistent with regard to why his cousin did not leave Bogota and join the Applicant in Riochacha; • The lack of corroborative evidence regarding the ownership of a second pharmacy and the sale of the first one; • The Applicant’s implausible and inconsistent testimony as to why his common law spouse did not leave Colombia with him; and, • The implausibility of the Applicant’s encounter with a stranger at a train station in New York, and, his decision to pay a stranger $5,000 to help him illegally cross the Canadian border.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD properly deferred to RPD’s credibility findings, which noted inconsistencies and lack of corroboration in the Applicant’s testimony.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Applicant’s testimony difficult, requiring repeated questioning.
propositions.quote: The RPD had the opportunity to hear the Applicant and appreciate the Applicant’s demeanor during his testimony. The RPD found that the Applicant’s testimony was difficult, as questions had to be put to the Applicant more than once.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Applicant’s testimony difficult and requiring repeated questioning.

propositions.text: The RAD independently assessed evidence and agreed with RPD’s lack of credibility findings on core narrative elements.
propositions.quote: The RAD, cognizant of the deference owed to the RPD, conducted its own assessment of the evidence as a whole. The RAD agreed with the findings of lack of credibility of the Applicant; as it found that the Applicant lacked credibility on essential elements of his narrative regarding threats allegedly made by the FARC to himself and his common law spouse.

propositions.text: Reasonableness review of RAD’s decision looks at reasons as a whole, not each point individually.
propositions.quote: In assessing whether the RAD’s decision to uphold RPD’s credibility findings is reasonable, the Court must look at the RAD’s reasons as a whole; its analysis does not involve determining whether each point in its reasoning meets the reasonableness standard (Jarada v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2005 FC 409; Uwitonze v Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), 2012 FC 61).

propositions.text: Given numerous discrepancies, it was reasonable for RAD to find the Applicant lacked credibility on core narrative elements.
propositions.quote: Given the numerous and important discrepancies raised by the RPD in its decision, it was reasonable for the RAD to find that the Applicant lacked credibility on core elements of his narrative.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD reasonably upheld RPD’s lack of credibility findings after independent assessment of evidence as a whole.

propositions.text: The RPD made additional credibility findings against the Applicant beyond initial assessment.
propositions.quote: the RPD did not stop its assessment of RPD’s decision at that point; it made additional credibility findings against the Applicant

propositions.text: The RAD independently assessed evidence and excluded weight of some evidence including the police report.
propositions.quote: The RAD, in conducting its independent assessment of the evidence, held that numerous evidence, including the police report, should not be given weight

propositions.text: If RAD only reviewed and agreed with RPD's findings on evidence adequacy, matter would end.
propositions.quote: Had the RAD simply reviewed the findings of the RPD as to the adequacy of the Applicant's evidence and agreed with it, that would have ended the matter

propositions.text: The RAD made independent credibility findings against the Applicant on four grounds.
propositions.quote: the RAD, as pointed out by the Respondent in its Memorandum of Facts, independently made numerous findings regarding the Applicant’s credibility

propositions.text: Applicant failed to produce crucial documents corroborating sale of first pharmacy despite producing other documents.
propositions.quote: The Applicant failed to produce crucial documents to corroborate his claim regarding the sale of his first pharmacy even though he produced several other documents

propositions.text: Applicant gave inconsistent testimony about his cousin before the RPD.
propositions.quote: The inconsistent testimony of the Applicant regarding his cousin before the RPD

propositions.text: Applicant moved to areas with active FARC child recruitment despite evidence FARC weakened in Colombia.
propositions.quote: The Applicant moved to two areas where the FARC is actively recruiting children, even though documentary evidence suggest that the FARC has been weakened in Colombia

propositions.text: Police report submitted by Applicant did not conform to country conditions documents.
propositions.quote: The police report submitted by the Applicant in support of his claim did not appear to conform to the descriptions found in the country conditions documents

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD made additional credibility findings; RAD independently assessed evidence and excluded some; prior authority says RAD agreeing with RPD ends matter; RAD made four independent credibility findings as respondent argues.

propositions.text: RAD may make independent credibility findings without applicant's input if it did not ignore contradictory evidence or make unknown findings.
propositions.quote: even if the RAD made independent findings of credibility against an applicant, without putting it before the applicant and giving him or her the opportunity to make submissions, the RAD’s decision may still be reasonable

propositions.text: RAD decision reasonable if it did not ignore contradictory evidence or make unknown findings to applicant.
propositions.quote: the RAD did not ignore contradictory evidence on the record or make additional findings on issues unknown to the applicant

propositions.text: This exception does not apply here because RAD raised doubts about police report genuineness not discussed by RPD or put to Applicant.
propositions.quote: the Court does not find that this exception applies... RAD independently held that the police report does not appear to conform to the normally followed process... an issue which was not discussed by the RPD, and, neither put forth to the Applicant

propositions.text: A breach of procedural fairness occurred due to RAD's undisclosed doubts about police report.
propositions.quote: As a result, the Court finds that a breach of procedural fairness occurred

paragraphs.summary: Prior authority allows RAD independent findings if applicant informed; court finds exception does not apply here as RAD raised undisclosed doubts about police report, breaching fairness.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is granted.
propositions.quote: the application for judicial review is granted

propositions.text: File is sent back to RAD for reassessment by a differently constituted panel.
propositions.quote: the file be sent to the RAD for assessment anew by a differently constituted panel

propositions.text: No serious question of general importance to certify.
propositions.quote: There is no serious question of general importance to be certified

paragraphs.summary: The court grants judicial review, remands file to RAD for new assessment, and declines to certify a serious question of general importance.
